_: Lines for testenv/perf/keys.mjs (just keys-budget --real <port>): from a key pressed as real input to the first frame that draws the rows it asks for (rowsMs, the median of the presses), and how many frames after that moved or took away a row drawn on screen (moved). Björn's line is 100 ms at 1x and 200 ms at 4x, measured in headless Chrome on an M2 Pro over the saved scale database through a release build of examples/headless_ipc.rs. The broad-filters pass of PR #2479 (2026-11-13) measured 103 to 132 ms at 1x and set these lines at 130 to 160. The broad-keys pass of the same day brought every key under his line, so the 1x lines are his line: 71, 83, 64 and 91 ms measured as the median of seven presses, 93 to 104 at 4x. Those were taken with other agents' test runs and browsers on the machine, which a press feels: the backend's own read of a letter was 54 ms asked alone and 65 to 75 during a run, and single presses ran 20 ms either side of the median. A second run of five presses read 96, 75, 67 and 96. So a miss by a few ms on a loaded machine is the machine; read the backend's --timings beside it. docs/decisions/2026-11-13-a-broad-key-answers-in-a-frame-or-two.md has both passes. The Windows pass (2026-11-14) added the expanded board (tickets-expanded-*: every column's Show more pressed four times, 1,243 cards on the scale database): 136 to 142 ms at 1x and 207 to 225 at 4x with every card drawn, 89 to 106 and 106 to 112 with each column windowed. Its read of 250 cards a column answers at 77 to 98 ms at 1x, which the page cannot go under, so its 1x line is the measure with margin, 115, not his 100; 140 at 4x. docs/decisions/2026-11-14-what-the-windows-pass-found.md. The render-cost pass (2026-11-14) added Björn's 6x line: every key's rows drawn within 200 ms at CPU 6x; docs/decisions/2026-11-14-what-a-page-costs-to-build.md. The one-letter pass (2026-11-15) answers one character under Everything by names, off an index, and draws an answer's first 24 rows in the frame it lands: 84, 121 and 125 ms before at 1x, 4x and 6x, 42, 63 and 94 after (medians of three rounds of seven presses, the two builds alternated, a load average of 7 to 13). His key targets are 100, 100 and 200 on his PC, where the page's share is as large as the Mac's and the read about 1.5 times it, so everything-letter's lines are 70, 100 and 130: the Mac with room for the machine. A run with other agents' builds on the cores read 74 at 1x; knobas-search's own tests hold the statement to the index, so a miss here is the page or the machine. docs/decisions/2026-11-15-one-letter-is-answered-by-names.md. The two-letters pass (2026-11-16) answers the second and the third letter of a word the same way, where each was ranked as a word: everything-two-letters and everything-three-letters press the next letter into a box that holds the letters before. 96, 126 and 145 ms before at 1x, 4x and 6x for the second letter and 89, 103 and 118 for the third, 34, 61 and 73 and 31, 59 and 73 after (medians of three rounds of seven presses, the two builds alternated, a load average of 4 to 8). Their lines are one letter's, 70, 100 and 130. Every press changes what the list draws: one that asks for the rows already drawn (le, then d) leaves the probe no frame to time. docs/decisions/2026-11-16-two-letters-by-names-and-keys-wait-for-their-answer.md. The long-words pass (2026-11-16) counts a query before it answers it and, where more than 2,000 rows hold it, answers by the rows it names and each kind's newest rows whose text holds it, where every match was ranked: everything-four-letters, everything-five-letters and everything-word press the fourth letter, the fifth and the last of words half the scale mirror holds. 75, 98 and 119 ms before at 1x, 4x and 6x for the fourth letter, 76, 83 and 99 for the fifth and 72, 93 and 103 for a word's last, 49, 57 and 78, 45, 52 and 68 and 36, 55 and 69 after (two rounds of seven presses, the two builds alternated, a load average of 2 to 6). Their lines are the letters', 70, 100 and 130. docs/decisions/2026-11-16-a-word-many-rows-hold.md. Docs' spaces filter (PR #2479, 2026-11-17): docs-spaces-letter and docs-spaces-two-letters press a letter into the rail's filter of spaces, which reads nothing and narrows what Docs holds; their lines are Björn's key targets, 100, 100 and 200 ms at 1x, 4x and 6x. docs/decisions/2026-11-17-where-docs-opens-and-the-spaces-it-hides.md.
